threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think every café is just a coffee shop, not realizing half of them serve six types of avocado toast.
Caught a group of teenagers on the N35 singing classic grime tracks, off-key but loud. Their energy lit up the damp night. Brixton never sleeps.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Caught a bus the other day, and the driver gave a whole history lesson about the route. Only in Neukölln do you get your daily dose of local lore with your ride.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a Kiez that turns a former tram depot into a pop-up beach club. Sand, cocktails, and a DJ—it's a summer vibe like no other.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they seamlessly switch from English to Spanglish while ordering tacos at La Taqueria without missing a beat.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni bus today where the driver paused for a street performer—everyone on board started clapping. Only in SF do you jam out on your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the local bars are just for sipping cocktails, but really, we gather over a simple glass of vermut and good conversation.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle to navigate the narrow, winding streets, often stopping to consult maps or smartphones every few minutes.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stoke Newington Church Street' instead of just 'the Church Street' like everyone else here.
Saw a lad playing his sax on the 21 last night—bus driver stopped the whole thing just to listen, like we were in a jazz club for a moment.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The aroma of grilled corn wafting from the market on Hermannplatz while a neighbor argues passionately with a street musician—that’s when I knew.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can catch a late-night tram here with DJ sets onboard. It's like a rolling party—only in Berlin do you ride along to live beats while cruising the streets.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: If they know which taco truck to hit after midnight, they’re local. If they say 'taco' instead of 'tacos,' they’re definitely just here for a gig.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy juggling on the bus while discussing the latest BART delays. Classic SF—chaos mixed with creativity, even when transit's a mess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks and plazas, but the real charm lies in the tiny, tucked-away bars where the locals laugh until dawn.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by their confused looks while trying to navigate the metro map—especially when they attempt to pronounce 'L2'.
